blocks.x: Connected service on machine twins — first-time-fix up 19 points and service contract margin up 8 points
an equipment OEM whose service arm was its growth story and its margin problem: every second visit was a part that wasn't on the truck. Figures are the client's own, shared with permission.
The baseline quarter counted the second visits: 54% first-time-fix, service contract margin eroding with every warranty year, and diagnostic knowledge trapped in the tenure of senior field engineers.
Machines reported errors as codes; field engineers arrived with the code and left with a story. Parts planning ran on generic failure rates that never matched the installed base's actual behavior.

We gave each machine a twin: telemetry and service history resolved per serial number, diagnostic paths encoded from senior engineers' reasoning and kept current by their review, fault-to-part resolution mapped so dispatch stages the right kit, and the customer portal booking against real availability. New engineers inherit the reasoning; margins inherit the fix rate.
